p9_b0.ocr: The study by Ekangaki and Chung [5] in 2005 involved a sample size of 450 cancer patients under chemotherapy in two various age-gender groups, utilizing a case-control design, and concluded that the application of histamines, phenothiazines, butyrophenones, and anticholinergics to cope with CINV in chemotherapy brings about side effects. Sirin and Flynn [6] in 2013 examined 52 cancer patients under chemotherapy in two various age-gender groups and found that CINV was reduced by about 13.8% in the group receiving dimenhydrinate as compared to placebo.

p9_b1.ocr: Pierce and Lin [7] in 2013 studied 85 over 30-year-old men with prostate cancer under chemotherapy, discovering that prescribing dimenhydrinate reduced their CINV compared to the control group. Sheanakul et al. [8] in 2011 analyzed 30 below 60-year-old cancer patients under chemotherapy in two gender groups and determined that the continuous injection of midazolam reduced pain and CINV. Apfel et al. [9] in 2012 focused on 23 cancer patients aged 15–50 under chemotherapy and found that cinnarizine controls and reduces CINV.
